13: By enabling the "Fighters transfer cargo" preference, drones and fighters in your fleet will transfer cargo to their parent carrier if there is cargo space in the carrier. If a fighter cargo hold is full then it will return to the carrier automatically.
14: Drones and fighters will transfer cargo upon docking with their carrier for any reason.
18: Your ship does not jump until you release the jump key. Once you have escorts, you can hold the key to get them ready to jump, then release it to have them all jump simultaneously.
19: When you reach a new system, you can press <Land on planet / station> to land on any inhabited planets that are there.
20: Also, don't worry about crashing into asteroids or other ships; your ship will fly safely below or above them.
21: Here, you can buy new equipment for your ship. Your ship has a limited amount of "outfit space," and most outfits use up some of that space.
22: Some types of outfits have other requirements as well. For example, only some of your outfit space can be used for engines or weapons; this is your ship's "engine capacity" and "weapon capacity." Guns and missile launchers also require a free "gun port," and turrets require a free "turret mount." Also, missiles can only be bought if you have the right launcher installed.
23: Use your scroll wheel or click and drag, to scroll the view.
24: As in the trading and shipyard panels, you can hold down Shift, Control, or Alt to buy, sell, or move 5, 20, or 500 of an outfit at once, or multiple keys for larger amounts.
25: You can also press F to search the outfitter for a specific item.
26: Here, you can buy new ships.
27: Use your scroll wheel or click and drag, to scroll the view.
28: As in the trading and outfitter panels, you can hold down Shift, Control, or Alt to buy 5, 20, or 500 ships at once, or multiple keys for larger amounts.
29: You can use the shortcuts B to Buy, S to Sell the ship and outfits, and R to sell the ship and retain the outfits if the planet has an outfitter.
30: You can also press F to search the shipyard for a specific ship.
31: Sometimes you may want to buy outfits directly into your cargo hold instead of having them installed.
32: You can use the following keyboard shortcuts or the buttons to move outfits around:
34: - "S" to sell outfits from cargo, planetary storage, or your ship (in that order)
35: - "I" to install outfits from cargo and/or storage (in that order)
36: - "U" to uninstall outfits from your ship and leave them in planetary storage, or unload outfits from cargo to planetary storage (in that order)
37: - "C" to move outfits from planetary storage and/or the outfitter (after paying) and move them into cargo
38: - "R" to move outfits from your cargo hold (if any are there) or else to uninstall to planetary storage
39: Outfits that are in your cargo hold can be installed at any outfitter without cost.
40: Using planetary storage can be useful for if you want to shuffle outfits between ships, store outfits for future use, or simply try different outfits.
41: Outfits that are in planetary storage or cargo can be installed without cost.
42: If you sell an outfit at an outfitter, then you can immediately buy it back for the same price that you sold it, so long as you do not leave the planet.
43: This means that you do not necessarily need to worry about uninstalling outfits into planetary storage when you are changing outfits around.
44: You can manage outfits on multiple ships at the same time. Ctrl+click a ship icon to add it to your selection. You can also use Shift+click to select a range of ships.
45: When you have more than one ship selected, you can install or remove outfits from all of those ships at once. Additionally, all selected ships with the currently selected outfit installed are marked with a pointer next to their sidebar icon.
46: Escorts can be saved into control groups by pressing a number key while holding Control. All selected escorts will then be bound to that number key, and can be selected again at any time by pressing it.
47: Ship group management can be done while flying around or while in the shipyard, outfitter, or player info panel.
48: Oops! You just ran out of fuel in an uninhabited star system. Fortunately, other ships are willing to help you.
49: Press <Select next ship> to cycle through all the ships in this system. When you have a friendly one selected, press <Talk to selected ship> to hail it. You can then ask for help, and if it has fuel to spare it will fly over and transfer fuel to your ship. This is easiest for the other ship to do if your ship is nearly stationary.
50: This is the trading panel. Earn money by buying commodities at a low price in one system, and selling at a higher price elsewhere. To view your map of commodity prices in other systems, press <View star map>. To buy or sell, click on [buy] or [sell], or select a line with the up and down arrows and press "+" or "-" (or Enter and Delete).
51: You can buy 5 tons at once by holding down Shift, 20 by holding down Control, 500 by holding down Alt, or larger amounts at a time by holding down two keys at once, or even all three.
52: Sell other items in your cargo hold with the buttons to the left. "Sell Minables" sells materials mined from asteroids and other space debris. "Sell Outfits" sells all the other outfits present in cargo hold.
53: This ship is disabled and needs your help to patch them up! Pressing <Board selected ship> will fly you to their ship and get them up and running again. Just be sure to do it when no one is trying to kill you, or they could get caught in the crossfire!
54: You've enabled controlling your ship with your mouse.
55: The nose of your ship will always turn toward your mouse pointer.
56: <Forward thrust> is used to thrust forward.
58: Right mouse click will fire primary weapons.
59: <Mouse turning (hold)> will toggle mouse turning while it is held.
60: The "go to and hold" command is remapped from the right mouse button to the middle one.
